## Intent
Hypothesis: a branchless blend for the death/respawn verdict, keeping the decision in registers with no intermediate storage, can avoid branch misprediction and stream the 68 B/p AoS layout close to the memory floor.

## Layout & approach
The 68 B/p AoS layout offers 32 hot bytes per particle to loop 1 (age+pos+seed+vel, 47%) and 28 to loop 2 (color+pos, 41%); the remaining 53–59% is dead weight dragged through every cache-line fill. With no intermediate storage the death verdict stays in registers, which is the one structural advantage — but the approach then scatters results back via byte-granular stores (×13 in loop 1, ×16 in loop 2), so the useful-bandwidth fraction is further eroded by sub-word writes that cannot coalesce into full-line stores. Working set spills L1d at N≈481, L2 at N≈7710, L3 at N≈246723; given the 47%/41% hot fractions, the effective hot working set crosses those thresholds even sooner.

## Cache saturation
The ns/p curve is strikingly flat: at q=0.01 it rises only from 20.3 (N=320, L1d) to 24.9 (N=10M, DRAM) — a 1.23× increase across the entire cache hierarchy. No sharp knee appears at any spill: L1d→L2 (N≈481→720) is noise (20.3→20.5), L2→L3 (N≈7700→10000) is flat (23.3→23.2), and L3→DRAM (N≈160000→250000) adds only ~1 ns/p (22.8→23.8). This flatness signals overhead-bound behavior, not bandwidth-bound: the same per-particle scatter and branch cost dominates regardless of cache level, so cache residence barely matters.

## Bandwidth
Achieved bandwidth is 2.1–3.4 GB/s against the 12.69 GB/s ceiling — 17–27% of ceiling — while the memory floor of 5.359 ns/p means the algo runs at 3.7–6.0× the irreducible memory time. The verdict is overhead- and branch-bound, not bandwidth-bound. Against baseline the algo is marginally faster at low q (0.917× at q=0.01, N=320) but converges to parity at DRAM scales (0.976–0.999× at N≥250000). Against the winner it loses everywhere: 2.74× slower at q=0.01 N=320, widening to 3.35× at N=160000, then narrowing to 2.38× at N=10M as the winner also hits DRAM. Death rate is the equalizer — at q=0.5 the gap compresses to 1.70–1.91× because branch_flush rises to 15.9% and the winner's vectorization advantage shrinks, but blend still never catches up.

## Assembly
Loop 1 shows partial vectorization: `vmovups` for 16 B loads, `vmulps`/`vaddps` for 4-lane FP, but interleaved with scalar `vmulss`/`vaddss` and component shuffles (`vinsertps`, `vshufps`) that the stride-68 AoS layout forces. The death decision uses `vucomiss` + `jbe`/`je` — still branchy despite the "blend" label, with 7 conditional branches per iteration. Byte-granular scatter appears as `movzx` + `mov BYTE PTR` stores (×13). Loop 2 is worse: 21 conditional branches, purely scalar FP (×14), `cmovae`-based selects (×12) that avoid misprediction but still cannot stream, and 16 byte-granular scatters. Only 26 of 383 instructions are vector — the AoS shuffles consume the vectorization benefit and explain why achieved bandwidth stalls at 21% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — 0.92–1.0× of baseline (barely matching naive scalar) and 1.7–3.4× slower than the winner at every N×q point. At q=0.01, N=10M: 24.9 ns/p vs the 5.359 floor (4.7× overhead) and 2.38× the winner. The "blend" does not eliminate branches (7–21 per loop, branch_flush 12–16%), partial vectorization is undermined by AoS shuffles, and byte-granular scatter (×13–16) prevents streaming — the algo is overhead-bound at every cache regime.
